marker: # unit_length is the published repeat unit length U, ref_repeats the published repeat number N and
# ref_size the expected product in CO92 that the source table gives, all three taken from the table
# unchanged. In silico PCR with these primers in the CO92 assembly GCA_000009065.1 reproduces every
# one of the 25 published products exactly, outer primer edge to outer primer edge: one product per
# locus, all on the chromosome AL590842.1, all searchable at hash word size 11, none needing the
# rescue pass and none with a primer mismatch. This is a complete check of the published sizes.
# The full locus name in the label column gives the position of the locus in the CO92 chromosome in
# kb, and all 25 products start at that position, for example ms01 (yp0120ms01) at 120578 and ms09
# (yp3057ms09) at 3057920. The locus identity is therefore confirmed independently of the size.
# ms40 is the one internal inconsistency in the source: its expected product is 214 bp while its
# published size range is 220-240 bp, which excludes it. The measurement agrees with 214 bp, so the
# size is taken as published and the range is treated as the error.
# patterns is N/A at every locus, so the tandem array cross-check is off throughout and alleles rest
# on amplicon length alone, which is how this panel is numbered. The source table gives no repeat
# motifs, and the published repeat number is not a count of whole units in CO92: the arrays are
# degenerate, which the source itself records as a conservation of 59 to 97 per cent per locus, and
# at no locus does the longest run of adjacent units within that conservation reach N. The run is
# shorter than N at 24 of the 25 loci, by one unit at ms01, ms70 and ms74 and by five or more at
# ms15, ms21, ms41, ms45, ms46, ms51, ms54 and ms06, and only ms62 exceeds it, with eight runs of a
# poly-T rich 9 bp unit against the published seven. Storing a motif would therefore make every
# Repeat detection in the CO92 amplicons does reproduce the published unit length at 21 of the 25
# loci, which is the strongest check the source allows on U. Four do not: ms15 gives 16 bp against
# the published 15, ms51 gives 21 against 18, ms46 gives a 7 bp unit (five perfect copies of
# AATAGTT) against the published 17, and ms06 and ms54 give no unit at all, their arrays being too
# diverged (conservation 64 and 82 per cent, with a 60 bp and a 22 bp unit). An allele of ms46 or
# ms51 that disagrees with a database is worth checking against the unit length first.
